findings.title: validateHandlerOrder missing zero-price check allows overflow bypass of pricing bounds (CP-003)
findings.description: SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96() returns 0 on uint160 overflow (line 52). In AMMStandardHook._enforceTokenHooks(), this is caught by an explicit zero check (line 847). However, AMMStandardHook.validateHandlerOrder() (line 215) does NOT have this zero check. If minSqrtPriceX96 == 0 (no minimum bound set), the zero return value passes the bounds check, allowing a swap at an undefined price.
findings.impact: CLOB handler orders via CLOBTransferHandler._validateTokenHooks() could bypass pricing bounds if token amounts cause computeRatioX96 overflow and no minimum bound is configured. Attacker could execute trades at manipulated effective prices.
findings.proof_sketch: 1. computeRatioX96(very_large_amount1, 1) → overflow → returns 0. 2. validateHandlerOrder called with sqrtPriceX96=0. 3. If minSqrtPriceX96==0, check `0 != 0 && 0 < min` is false → passes. 4. If maxSqrtPriceX96 != 0, check `0 > max` is false → passes. Both bounds bypassed.
findings.victim: Liquidity providers in pools with CLOB handler and token hooks that use validateHandlerOrder without minimum pricing bound
findings.extractable_value: Depends on pool liquidity depth. Constrained by CLOB order book pricing — attacker cannot freely choose both amounts, they come from CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput(). Likely low practical EV due to CLOB constraints.
attack_sequence: 1. Find pool pair where token has validateHandlerOrderHook=true and minSqrtPriceX96==0
2. Create CLOB order with extreme price ratio that causes computeRatioX96 overflow
3. Execute order via CLOBTransferHandler — validateHandlerOrder receives sqrtPriceX96=0
4. Zero passes both min and max bounds checks
5. Order executes at price outside intended bounds
prerequisites: Amount ratio that causes computeRatioX96 to overflow uint160

findings.title: setTokenSettings passes unmodified settings to hook sync — initialized field may be false (CP-004)
findings.description: CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.setTokenSettings() creates memSettings with initialized=true for registry storage (line 377-378) but passes original calldata settings (without initialized=true) to hook sync at line 397. AMMStandardHook.registryUpdateTokenSettings() stores settings with potentially initialized=false (line 522). This causes a sync gap between registry and hook cached state.
findings.impact: Low. AMMStandardHook._getOrFetchTokenSettings() self-heals: when initialized=false, it re-fetches from registry and re-caches correctly (lines 908-914). Window of inconsistency is brief (until next swap or hook call on that token). No funds at risk — only causes an unnecessary SLOAD on next access.
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Creator calls setTokenSettings(token, settings) with settings.initialized=false. 2. Registry stores with initialized=true. 3. Hook stores with initialized=false. 4. Next _getOrFetchTokenSettings(token) sees initialized=false → re-fetches from registry → gets correct settings → re-caches with initialized=true.
findings.extractable_value: 0 — no extraction path. Extra SLOAD cost per affected token on next access.
attack_sequence: 1. Admin calls setTokenSettings with initialized=false in settings struct
2. Registry caches with initialized=true, hook caches with initialized=false
3. Brief window where hook has stale state
prerequisites: Admin/owner must call setTokenSettings with initialized=false

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Tick crossing at exact boundary → liquidity not properly added/removed
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Standard Uniswap V3 logic. Tick crossing check uses == comparison. getNextSqrtPriceFromInput rounds conservatively. Battle-tested pattern.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Fixed height split rounds to zero on one side → free tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Proportional split uses mulDivRoundingUp (user pays more), output uses calculateFixedSwapByRatioRoundingDown (user gets less). Both favor protocol. Zero-value swaps revert at line 1656.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: 100% fee asymmetry → extract value
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known design (L-04). 100% input fee → amountRemainingLessFee=0 → no swap. Output rejects 100% fee. No extraction.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: swapExtraData != 32 bytes → unexpected price movement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known issue (L-01). Defaults to widest price limit. AMM's limitAmount provides slippage protection separately.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: uint256 truncation on cast to uint128 in safe increment/decrement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Assembly implementations check overflow correctly. shr(128, sum) > 0 catches overflow. Input values from uint128 storage slots.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Division before multiplication truncates intermediate → pay less fee
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All fee calculations use FullMath.mulDiv with 512-bit intermediate products. No precision loss.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Assembly calldataload without masking → dirty high bits
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Uses calldatacopy for structured data, not arbitrary calldataload. Address values masked where needed.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: ABI encoding attacks, returndata corruption, memory pointer corruption
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Solidity 0.8.24 strict mode. No raw returndatacopy without length checks. Memory-safe assembly blocks.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Dust-loop extraction (100+ tiny swaps to harvest rounding)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Dust from rounding goes to pool (dust0/dust1), distributed to LPs. Output rounds DOWN, input rounds UP — attacker loses on each swap plus fees.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Operator precedence bug at FixedHelper:799 (a | b == 0)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Verified via Forge test: Solidity | binds tighter than ==, so a | b == 0 evaluates as (a | b) == 0. Correct behavior.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Operator precedence bug at FixedHelper:1469 (amount0 | amount1 > type(uint128).max)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Solidity | has higher precedence than >. Evaluates as (amount0 | amount1) > type(uint128).max. Guard works correctly.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: SingleProviderHelper roundtrip precision leak (input→output→input)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Two-step sqrt decomposition with correct rounding: input mulDiv down twice, output mulDivRoundingUp twice. Roundtrip preserves or exceeds original.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper swapByInput→swapByOutput fallback double-charges fees
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fallback recalculates amountIn from scratch, not from fee-deducted amount. Line 917 check prevents exceeding original input.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Cross-boundary fee flow mismatch between pool types and AMMModule
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: validateProtocolFees uses same mulDiv formula as pool types. Rounding differences favor protocol (both round down for protocol share).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: DynamicPoolType permissionless access → state manipulation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: globalState keyed by msg.sender. Attacker calling directly creates isolated state AMM never reads.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: uint128 truncation in DynamicHelper._getTokensOwed
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: delta * liquidity bounded by total fees * Q128 / minLiquidity. Same as Uniswap V3, no practical overflow within uint256.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Forged hook caller — call hook directly with fake pool identity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: _requireCallerIsAMM() check on all hook entry points: AMMStandardHook.sol lines 110, 159, 253, 312, 940-942.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Transient-slot theft — stale DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known CP-001, by-design. Second beforeSwap call intentionally overwrites first. No exploitable stale state.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Permit mutation — replay with mutated feeOnTop/recipient
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop unsigned is known (rejected submission #8). limitAmount caps total exposure. Signer can't lose more than limitAmount.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Storage-slot collision via diamond proxy facets
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool types are external contracts called via regular calls, not delegatecall. State isolated by msg.sender. Diamond storage at 0x9A1D isolated.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Direct handler call — CLOBTransferHandler.executeSwap() bypasses pricing
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: msg.sender != AMM check at line 230 + nonReentrant guard. afterSwapRefund also guarded at line 316.

theft_theses.thesis: Overflow computeRatioX96 to return 0, bypass validateHandlerOrder pricing bounds on CLOB orders
theft_theses.victim: LPs in pools with CLOB handler and no minimum pricing bound

theft_theses.thesis: Exploit settings sync gap to execute swaps during window when hook has stale token settings
theft_theses.victim: Token creators relying on hook enforcement
theft_theses.asset: Token value via relaxed hook settings

theft_theses.thesis: Compound 100+ dust swaps in Fixed pool to harvest rounding differences from height split
